name: Transfer Pricing
title: Transfer Pricing
answer: Transfer pricing covers the prices charged between related legal entities for goods, services, intangibles, and financing. In an AI business this includes licenses for models, access to training data, cloud compute, and shared development of algorithms. The goal is to allocate profit to the jurisdictions where economic activity occurs, and tax authorities expect those allocations to match what independent parties would have agreed.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Transfer pricing covers the prices charged between related legal entities for goods, services, intangibles, and financing. In an AI business this includes licenses for models, access to training data, cloud compute, and shared development of algorithms. The goal is to allocate profit to the jurisdictions where economic activity occurs, and tax authorities expect those allocations to match what independent parties would have agreed.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: Transfer pricing work runs on the company's general ledger, intercompany agreements, and the systems that track where people, servers, and data are located. It also depends on external databases of comparable company financials and on tax provision software that consolidates entity level results. For AI assets, the infrastructure must capture usage logs, model version histories, and data lineage so that value can be tied to specific entities.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work begins with a functional analysis of who controls risks, owns intangibles, and performs key functions. Practitioners then choose a transfer pricing method such as comparable uncontrolled price, cost plus, or transactional net margin, and for highly integrated AI development a profit split is often used. Benchmarking against independent companies and documenting the economic assumptions are standard parts of the file.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Transfer pricing is governed by the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines and local country rules, with documentation typically split into a master file, local file, and country by country report. The main risks are double taxation, penalties for mispricing, and disputes between tax authorities, which can be managed through advance pricing agreements or mutual agreement procedures. Provenance matters because the data used to value intangibles and select comparables must be traceable and defensible under audit.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Tax authorities are increasing their focus on intangibles, data, and digital services, which puts AI related transfer pricing under more scrutiny. The spread of global minimum tax rules and Pillar One reallocation will change how residual profit is divided. Companies are moving toward real time intercompany pricing engines and more automated documentation, while tax authorities use their own analytics to spot mismatches between contracts, substance, and reported profit.
